milestones.name: Conformation handling and deliverables
milestones.description: The 3D splits are consumed correctly and every artifact the evaluation depends on is present, aligned with the inputs and internally consistent.

criteria.description: predictions.json carries gap predictions for the test split and for all three representations on the validation split, plus one element per hidden atom, all finite, correctly sized and not a constant.

denoised_coords.npz holds refined coordinates for every atom of the denoising split, with offsets matching the input file and geometry that stays within a refinement's distance of the perturbed input.
The ablation reports at least six runs covering 3D denoising pre-training on and off, geometry used and withheld, and at least three pre-training data scales, each with validation predictions.

milestones.name: Models and ablation
milestones.description: Two separately trained models were submitted rather than one wearing two names, and the ablation runs are distinct trainings whose effects are re-derived from their own predictions rather than reported.

criteria.description: The 3D encoder checkpoint loads and holds a trained network's worth of parameters and layers.
The 2D baseline checkpoint loads, is of substantial size, and is a different model from the 3D encoder rather than the same one resubmitted.
The 3D, 2D and 1D representations produce measurably different validation predictions.

Every ablation run is re-scored against held-out labels from its own submitted predictions, no two configurations produce near-identical predictions, and withholding geometry measurably degrades accuracy.
Runs that skip pre-training are re-scored against held-out labels and must be measurably worse, so the unlabelled corpus has to have been used rather than merely declared.

milestones.name: Invariance, geometry and representation comparison
milestones.description: The representation behaves the way an SE(3)-invariant 3D model must, the refinement improves real geometry, and the comparison against 1D and 2D baselines is measured on held-out labels rather than asserted.

criteria.description: Molecules that occur twice in the test split under independent rigid motions and atom permutations receive the same prediction, which a model reading raw coordinates cannot achieve.
Refined geometry is measurably closer to the reference conformation than the perturbed input it started from, under the same rigid alignment.
The 2D topology and 1D SMILES baselines are trained in good faith and reach sensible error on held-out labels rather than being strawmen.
The 3D representation outperforms both the 2D and the 1D baseline on the held-out validation labels.
analysis.md discusses the value of 3D pre-training against the 1D sequence and 2D topology representations and covers the ablation axes.

The bond-graph model predicts on a split shipping no coordinates and the sequence model on a split shipping nothing but SMILES, so each baseline is demonstrably a working model of its own modality rather than the 3D encoder relabelled.
